question: What is the sex ratio of India as per 2011 census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 943 females per 1000 males.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, the national sex ratio stood at 943 females per 1000 males, an improvement over 933 in the 2001 census. (लिंगानुपात — प्रति 1000 पुरुषों पर महिलाओं की संख्या)

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after independence, conducted under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 

• The state with the highest sex ratio in 2011 was Kerala (1084), and the lowest was Haryana (879).

 

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) in 2011 was 919 females per 1000 males, which is a separate and more worrying indicator than the overall sex ratio.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's population as per the 2011 Census was approximately 121 crore, making it the second most populous country in the world at the time.

 

• The overall literacy rate as per Census 2011 was 74.04% (82.14% male, 65.46% female).

 

NOTE

 

• 843 females per 1000 males (Option 1): This figure does not correspond to any official all-India census sex ratio.

 

• 643 females per 1000 males (Option 3): This is far below the actual recorded figure and does not match Census data.

 

• 743 females per 1000 males (Option 4): This is also incorrect and does not match the 2011 Census figure.

question: Which of the following is NOT a permanent wind?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Permanent winds (also called planetary winds) blow throughout the year in a fixed direction over large areas of the Earth, due to the global pressure belt system. (स्थायी पवनें)

 

• Trade winds, Westerlies, and Easterlies are all examples of permanent/planetary winds caused by the pressure differences between the equator and the poles.

 

• Loo is a strong, hot, dry, dust-laden local/seasonal wind that blows during the day in the summer months (April to June) over the Indo-Gangetic plains of North India — it is not a year-round, global wind system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of periodic/seasonal winds in India include the monsoon winds and land and sea breezes.

 

• Local winds are caused by local temperature and pressure differences and blow only for short durations or seasons, unlike permanent winds.

 

NOTE

 

• Westerlies (Option 1): Permanent winds blowing from the subtropical high-pressure belt towards the sub-polar low-pressure belt (roughly 30°–60° latitude) in both hemispheres.

 

• Easterlies (Option 3): Permanent winds blowing from the polar high-pressure areas towards the sub-polar low-pressure belt.

 

• Trade winds (Option 4): Permanent winds blowing from the subtropical high-pressure belts towards the equatorial low-pressure belt.

question: Graphical User Interface (GUI) was developed during which of the following generations of computer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fourth Generation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fourth Generation of computers (1971–present) is based on the microprocessor, which allowed computers to become small, fast, and affordable for personal use. (चतुर्थ पीढ़ी के कंप्यूटर)

 

• The Graphical User Interface (GUI) — using windows, icons, menus, and a pointer (WIMP) instead of text-based commands — was developed during this generation, pioneered at Xerox PARC and later popularised by the Apple Macintosh (1984) and Microsoft Windows.

 

• Fourth generation computers also introduced technologies like VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration), personal computers, and networking/the Internet.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• First generation computers (1940s–1950s) used vacuum tubes; Second generation (1950s–60s) used transistors; Third generation (1960s–70s) used integrated circuits (ICs).

 

• The Fifth generation of computers is based on Artificial Intelligence.

 

NOTE

 

• Second Generation (Option 2): Characterised by transistors, and used assembly language/early high-level languages, not GUIs.

 

• First Generation (Option 3): Used vacuum tubes and machine language; input/output was via punched cards, with no graphical interface.

 

• Third Generation (Option 4): Characterised by integrated circuits (ICs); interaction was largely through keyboards and text-based operating systems.

question: In July 2022, who among the following has notified the detailed framework for Social Stock Exchange (SSE)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SEBI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) notified the detailed regulatory framework for the Social Stock Exchange (SSE) on 25 July 2022, through amendments to the ICDR and LODR Regulations. (सामाजिक स्टॉक एक्सचेंज)

 

• The SSE is a novel concept allowing social enterprises and non-profit organisations to raise funds from the public through a stock-exchange-like mechanism, functioning as a separate segment of existing stock exchanges (BSE/NSE).

 

• A SEBI-appointed working group, chaired by Ishaat Hussain, had earlier recommended the framework for setting up the SSE in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NSE received in-principle approval to set up its Social Stock Exchange as a separate segment.

 

• SEBI is the primary regulator of the securities market in India, established in 1988 and given statutory powers under the SEBI Act, 1992.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Corporate Affairs (Option 1): Regulates corporate affairs and company law in India but did not notify the SSE framework.

 

• RBI (Option 2): The Reserve Bank of India regulates banking and monetary policy, not the securities/stock exchange framework.

 

• NITI Aayog (Option 4): A policy think tank of the Government of India; it does not issue regulatory frameworks for stock exchanges.

question: “Statue of Equality” has been inaugurated in Hyderabad in the memory of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saint Ramanujacharya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "Statue of Equality", a 216-feet tall statue, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 5 February 2022 at Shamshabad, near Hyderabad, Telangana. (समानता की प्रतिमा — रामानुजाचार्य की स्मृति में)

 

• It commemorates Saint Ramanujacharya, the 11th-century Vaishnavite saint and philosopher who propounded the philosophy of Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism) and preached social equality irrespective of caste, creed, or gender.

 

• The statue is made of a panchaloha (five-metal) alloy of gold, silver, copper, brass, and zinc, and stands on a base building called "Bhadra Vedi".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The statue was consecrated as part of the Sri Ramanuja 1000th birth anniversary celebrations.

 

• Ramanujacharya is credited with reviving and spreading the Sri Vaishnavism tradition across India.

 

NOTE

 

• Swami Vivekananda (Option 2): A 19th-century monk and key figure of the Ramakrishna Mission who introduced Vedanta and Yoga to the West; not connected to this statue.

 

• Swami Dayananda (Option 3): Founder of the Arya Samaj (1875), an important 19th-century Hindu reform movement leader; unrelated to the Hyderabad statue.

 

• Shri Ravi Das (Option 4): A 15th-century mystic poet-saint of the Bhakti movement, revered particularly in North India; not linked to the "Statue of Equality".

question: In which of the following cities of the Indus valley civilization has a dockyard been found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lothal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lothal, located in present-day Gujarat on the Bhogava river (a tributary of the Sabarmati), is famous for having the world's earliest known artificial dockyard, indicating its importance as a maritime trade centre of the Indus Valley Civilization. (लोथल — गोदी/बंदरगाह)

 

• Lothal was excavated by S.R. Rao in 1954–55.

 

• Other notable finds at Lothal include a granary, evidence of bead-making industry, and a terracotta model of a ship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lothal falls under the Harappan (Mature Harappan) phase of the Indus Valley Civilization, dated roughly to 2400 BCE.

 

• It is part of the tentative UNESCO World Heritage list under "Harappan Cities".

 

NOTE

 

• Chanhudaro (Option 2): Located in Sindh, Pakistan; known for bead-making and being the only major Harappan site without a citadel; no dockyard found here.

 

• Kalibangan (Option 3): Located in Rajasthan; known for the earliest evidence of a ploughed field and fire altars; no dockyard found here.

 

• Dholavira (Option 4): Located in Gujarat (Kutch); known for its unique water conservation/reservoir system and three-part town planning; no dockyard has been found here.

question: A free-market economy is a crucial aspect of __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Capitalism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A free-market economy, where prices, production, and distribution of goods are determined by the forces of demand and supply with minimal government intervention, is a defining/crucial feature of capitalism. (पूँजीवाद — मुक्त बाज़ार अर्थव्यवस्था)

 

• Under capitalism, the means of production (land, capital, factories) are privately owned, and individuals operate for profit in a competitive market.

 

• Capitalism contrasts with socialism, where the means of production are collectively or state-owned, and resource allocation is centrally planned rather than market-driven.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Adam Smith, in his work "The Wealth of Nations" (1776), is regarded as the father of modern capitalist/free-market economic thought, introducing the idea of the "invisible hand".

 

• A mixed economy (like India's) combines elements of both free-market capitalism and state planning/regulation.

 

NOTE

 

• Socialism (Option 1): An economic system based on collective or state ownership of the means of production and centrally planned allocation of resources, not a free market.

 

• Feudalism (Option 3): A medieval socio-economic system based on land ownership by lords, with peasants/serfs working the land in exchange for protection; not a market-based system.

 

• Functionalist (Option 4): "Functionalism" is a sociological theory about how institutions maintain social stability, not an economic system based on free markets.

question: What is the maximum number of electrons that the third orbit or M-shell can have?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in a given electron shell is given by the formula 2n², where n is the shell/orbit number. (इलेक्ट्रॉन कोश — अधिकतम इलेक्ट्रॉन क्षमता)

 

• For the third orbit (M-shell), n = 3, so the maximum number of electrons = 2 × 3² = 2 × 9 = 18.

 

• This rule (also called the Bohr-Bury scheme) governs the distribution of electrons in shells K, L, M, N, etc., corresponding to n = 1, 2, 3, 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The K-shell (n=1) holds a maximum of 2 electrons, and the L-shell (n=2) holds a maximum of 8 electrons.

 

• The outermost shell of an atom can hold a maximum of 8 electrons (octet rule), even if 2n² for that shell allows more.

 

NOTE

 

• 32 (Option 1): This is the maximum capacity of the fourth shell (N-shell, n=4), calculated as 2×4² = 32, not the third shell.

 

• 8 (Option 2): This is the maximum capacity of the second shell (L-shell, n=2), calculated as 2×2² = 8.

 

• 2 (Option 4): This is the maximum capacity of the first shell (K-shell, n=1), calculated as 2×1² = 2.

question: Qutub Minar is an example of ______ architecture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indo-Islamic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Qutub Minar, located in Delhi, is a 73-metre tall tapering tower built primarily of red sandstone and marble, and is a landmark example of Indo-Islamic architecture. (इंडो-इस्लामिक वास्तुकला)

 

• Its construction was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak (founder of the Delhi Sultanate/Mamluk dynasty) around 1199 CE and completed by his successor Iltutmish.

 

• Indo-Islamic architecture is a fusion style that blends indigenous Indian architectural elements (like corbelled arches, lotus motifs) with Islamic elements (like true arches, domes, minarets, calligraphy).

 

• The Qutub Minar complex, which also includes the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque and the Iron Pillar, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Qutub Minar is the tallest brick minaret in the world.

 

• Later Mughal-era Indo-Islamic structures include the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and Humayun's Tomb.

 

NOTE

 

• Dravidian (Option 2): A South Indian temple architecture style (with gopurams and vimanas), seen in temples like those at Thanjavur and Madurai; unrelated to the Qutub Minar.

 

• Sufi (Option 3): Refers to a mystical Islamic tradition/spiritual movement, not an architectural style associated with the Qutub Minar.

 

• Mauryan (Option 4): An ancient Indian architectural style (3rd century BCE), seen in Ashokan pillars and stupas like Sanchi; predates and is unrelated to the Qutub Minar.

question: Swami Vivekananda’s death anniversary is observed on ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is July 4.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Swami Vivekananda passed away on 4 July 1902 at Belur Math, West Bengal, at the young age of 39. (स्वामी विवेकानंद — पुण्यतिथि)

 

• He was born Narendranath Datta on 12 January 1863 in Kolkata; his birthday is observed in India as National Youth Day.

 

• He was a chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahansa and founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897, and is famed for his address at the Parliament of World's Religions, Chicago, in 1893.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vivekananda played a key role in introducing Vedanta and Yoga philosophy to Western audiences.

 

• The Ramakrishna Mission continues its work in education, healthcare, and social service across India.

 

NOTE

 

• July 1 (Option 1): Not associated with Swami Vivekananda; incidentally observed in India as National Doctors' Day.

 

• August 1 (Option 3): Not the correct date of Vivekananda's death.

 

• August 4 (Option 4): Not the correct date of Vivekananda's death.

question: The sensation of feeling full is because of a centre associated with hunger, which is in a separate part of the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Forebrain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The hunger centre and the satiety (feeling-full) centre are both located in the hypothalamus, which forms part of the forebrain. (अग्रमस्तिष्क — भूख एवं तृप्ति केंद्र)

 

• The hypothalamus regulates numerous vital functions such as hunger, thirst, body temperature, sleep, and emotional responses, acting as a link between the nervous and endocrine systems.

 

• The forebrain also includes the cerebrum (responsible for intelligence, memory, and voluntary actions) and the thalamus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The hindbrain comprises the cerebellum, pons, and medulla oblongata, controlling balance, posture, and involuntary functions like heartbeat and breathing.

 

• The midbrain relays visual and auditory information and helps control eye movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Pituitary gland (Option 1): An endocrine gland attached to the hypothalamus ("master gland") that secretes hormones; it is not itself the seat of the hunger/satiety centre.

 

• Midbrain (Option 2): Part of the brainstem involved in vision, hearing, and motor control; does not house the hunger/satiety centre.

 

• Hindbrain (Option 4): Controls balance, coordination, and autonomic functions like breathing and heart rate; does not house the hunger/satiety centre.

question:
Who among the following Indian athletes won a silver medal in 2022 Commonwealth Games?
I. Avinash Sable
II. Ravi Kumar Dahiya
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Avinash Sable won the silver medal in the men's 3000m steeplechase at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, missing gold by just 0.05 seconds — the best-ever Indian performance in this event at the CWG. (एवीनाश साबले — रजत पदक)

 

• Ravi Kumar Dahiya, the Tokyo Olympics silver medallist wrestler, won the gold medal (not silver) in the men's freestyle 57 kg wrestling category at the 2022 CWG.

 

• Therefore, statement I is correct and statement II is incorrect.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India finished the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games with a total of 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze), ranking 4th on the medal table.

 

• Indian wrestlers dominated the 2022 CWG, winning 6 gold medals in total, including Ravi Dahiya, Vinesh Phogat, and Naveen.

 

NOTE

 

• Both I and II (Option 1): Incorrect, since Ravi Kumar Dahiya won gold, not silver.

 

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, since Dahiya's medal was gold, and this option also wrongly excludes Sable's genuine silver.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect, since Avinash Sable did win a silver medal.

question: Who among the following was awarded with the 2022 Pulitzer Prize in Feature Photography category?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amit Dave.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Pulitzer Prize for Feature Photography was awarded to a team of four Reuters photographers — Danish Siddiqui (awarded posthumously), Adnan Abidi, Sanna Irshad Mattoo, and Amit Dave — for their harrowing coverage of India's COVID-19 crisis. (पुलित्जर पुरस्कार — फीचर फोटोग्राफी श्रेणी)

 

• Danish Siddiqui, a two-time Pulitzer winner, was killed in 2021 while covering the conflict in Afghanistan.

 

• The Pulitzer Prizes are prestigious American awards for achievements in journalism, literature, and musical composition, administered by Columbia University.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 Pulitzer Prize for International Reporting went to the staff of The New York Times for coverage of Russian attacks on civilians in Ukraine and Syria.

 

• Danish Siddiqui had earlier shared the 2018 Pulitzer Prize for Feature Photography for his coverage of the Rohingya refugee crisis.

 

NOTE

 

• K.R. Meera (Option 1): An acclaimed Malayalam-language novelist and short story writer, known for works like "Hangwoman"; not a Pulitzer photography winner.

 

• Syeda Hameed (Option 2): A former member of the Planning Commission of India and writer; not connected to the 2022 Pulitzer Prize.

 

• Bibek Debroy (Option 3): An economist and former Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the PM; not connected to the 2022 Pulitzer Prize.

question:
Which of the following is correct regarding the National Income?
I. Intermediate goods are not included in the calculation of national income.
II. Final goods are included in the calculation of national income.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National income is calculated using the value of only final goods and services produced in an economy during a given period. (राष्ट्रीय आय की गणना — केवल अंतिम वस्तुएँ)

 

• Intermediate goods (raw materials/semi-finished goods used up in producing other goods) are excluded from national income calculations to avoid the problem of double counting.

 

• Therefore, statement I (intermediate goods excluded) and statement II (final goods included) are both correct — they describe the same accounting principle from two sides.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• National income can also be measured by summing only the value added at each stage of production, which is mathematically equivalent to counting only final goods.

 

• GDP, GNP, NDP, and NNP are all key aggregates used in measuring a country's national income.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incomplete — it ignores that statement I is also a correct and complementary principle.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, as both statements accurately describe national income accounting principles.

 

• Only I (Option 3): Incomplete — it ignores that statement II is also correct.

question: Which of the following statement is NOT correct regarding Rutherford’s nuclear model of an atom?
option_1: The size of the nucleus is very large as compared to the size of the atom.
option_2: The electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular paths.
option_3: There is a positively charged centre in an atom called the nucleus.
option_4: Nearly all the mass of an atom resides in the nucleus.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The size of the nucleus is very large as compared to the size of the atom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Based on his famous gold foil (alpha particle scattering) experiment, Rutherford concluded that an atom has a tiny, dense, positively charged centre called the nucleus. (रदरफोर्ड परमाणु मॉडल — नाभिक)

 

• According to Rutherford's model, the nucleus is extremely small as compared to the overall size of the atom — most of the atom is empty space. This makes the given statement (that the nucleus is "very large" compared to the atom) factually incorrect.

 

• Rutherford also proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular orbits/paths, and that nearly all the mass of the atom is concentrated in the nucleus, both of which are true parts of his model.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A major limitation of Rutherford's model was that it could not explain the stability of the atom, since an accelerating (orbiting) electron should radiate energy and spiral into the nucleus — this was later addressed by Bohr's model.

 

• Rutherford's experiment disproved J.J. Thomson's earlier "plum pudding model" of the atom.

 

NOTE

 

• The electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular paths (Option 2): This is a correct part of Rutherford's model, describing the planetary-like motion of electrons.

 

• There is a positively charged centre in an atom called the nucleus (Option 3): This is correct and is the central conclusion of Rutherford's gold foil experiment.

 

• Nearly all the mass of an atom resides in the nucleus (Option 4): This is correct, as protons and neutrons (which carry almost all the atomic mass) are located in the nucleus.

question: Which of the following is a vulnerable species?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hornbill.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the IUCN Red List, the Great Hornbill (Buceros bicornis) has been classified as "Vulnerable" since 2018, primarily due to habitat loss from deforestation and hunting for its casque and feathers. (सुभेद्य प्रजाति — Vulnerable)

 

• The IUCN Red List categorises species (in decreasing order of threat) as: Critically Endangered → Endangered → Vulnerable → Near Threatened → Least Concern.

 

• The Asiatic/Asian elephant (Elephas maximus), by contrast, is classified as "Endangered" (a more severe category than Vulnerable) on the IUCN Red List, so it is not the correct answer to "which is a vulnerable species".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is home to several hornbill species, including the Great Hornbill, Malabar Pied Hornbill, and Indian Grey Hornbill; the Great Hornbill is the state bird of Kerala and Arunachal Pradesh.

 

• The Asiatic cheetah is classified as "Critically Endangered", the most severe IUCN category, with the last wild population confined to Iran.

 

NOTE

 

• Himalayan brown bear (Option 1): Its subspecies faces serious regional decline (locally assessed as critically endangered in parts of its Himalayan range), but the parent species (Ursus arctos) is globally assessed by the IUCN as "Least Concern", not "Vulnerable".

 

• Asiatic cheetah (Option 3): Classified as "Critically Endangered" on the IUCN Red List — a more severe category than "Vulnerable".

 

• Asiatic elephant (Option 4 — the PDF's marked answer): Classified as "Endangered" on the IUCN Red List, not "Vulnerable"; this appears to be an error in the official answer key.

question: Which of the following straits is located between the Java Sea and the Indian Ocean?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sunda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sunda Strait is located between the Indonesian islands of Java and Sumatra, connecting the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean. (सुंडा जलडमरूमध्य)

 

• It is a strategically important shipping route and is known for its strong currents and the volcanic island of Krakatoa, situated within it.

 

• The strait was made famous by the catastrophic 1883 eruption of Krakatoa, which triggered devastating tsunamis in the region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Indonesia consists of numerous straits due to its archipelagic geography, including the Sunda, Malacca, Lombok, and Makassar Straits.

 

• The Java Sea itself is a shallow sea bounded by the islands of Java, Sumatra, Borneo (Kalimantan), and Sulawesi.

 

NOTE

 

• Palk (Option 1): The Palk Strait lies between India (Tamil Nadu) and Sri Lanka, connecting the Palk Bay with the Bay of Bengal — unrelated to the Java Sea.

 

• Malacca (Option 2): The Malacca Strait lies between the Malay Peninsula and the Indonesian island of Sumatra, linking the Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean) to the South China Sea (Pacific Ocean) — it does not link to the Java Sea.

 

• Cook (Option 4): The Cook Strait separates the North and South Islands of New Zealand, connecting the Tasman Sea to the South Pacific Ocean — unrelated to the Java Sea/Indian Ocean.

question: Which country hosted the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is South Africa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2023 (the 8th edition) was hosted by South Africa, held from 10 to 26 February 2023. (आईसीसी महिला टी-20 विश्व कप)

 

• The final was played at Newlands Cricket Ground, Cape Town, where Australia defeated the host nation South Africa to win their sixth title.

 

• This was the first ICC Women's T20 World Cup hosted in Africa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India hosted the Women's Premier League (WPL), a franchise T20 league, starting in 2023, but not the ICC Women's T20 World Cup.

 

• The ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2022 had been hosted by Australia, won by England.

 

NOTE

 

• England (Option 1): Hosted the ICC Women's T20 World Cup in 2009, not 2023.

 

• Australia (Option 3): Hosted the ICC Women's T20 World Cup in 2020 and won the 2023 edition as a team, but did not host it.

 

• India (Option 4): Has hosted other ICC events (e.g., the Men's ODI World Cup 2023) but not the Women's T20 World Cup 2023.

question: Which of the following is NOT a type of paragraph formatting in MS-Word 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Precise.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• MS-Word provides four standard paragraph alignment options in its Home tab/Paragraph group: Left, Right, Centre, and Justify. (अनुच्छेद संरेखण)

 

• "Precise" is not a recognised type of paragraph formatting/alignment in MS-Word; it is not among the standard alignment buttons or paragraph settings.

 

• Justify alignment evenly distributes text so that both the left and right margins are straight, by adjusting spacing between words.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other paragraph formatting features in MS-Word include line spacing, indentation, and paragraph spacing (before/after).

 

• The default keyboard shortcuts for alignment in MS-Word are: Ctrl+L (Left), Ctrl+R (Right), Ctrl+E (Centre), and Ctrl+J (Justify).

 

NOTE

 

• Right (Option 1): A valid paragraph alignment option that aligns text along the right margin.

 

• Justify (Option 3): A valid paragraph alignment option that aligns text evenly along both left and right margins.

 

• Centre (Option 4): A valid paragraph alignment option that centres text between the left and right margins.

question: Aditi Mangaldas is a leading dancer & Choreographer in the classical Indian dance form of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aditi Mangaldas is a renowned Indian classical dancer and choreographer specialising in Kathak, trained under gurus Kumudini Lakhia and Birju Maharaj. (कथक नृत्य)

 

• She is the founder of the "Drishtikon Dance Foundation", based in New Delhi, and is known for blending traditional Kathak with contemporary choreography.

 

• She has received numerous honours for her contribution to Indian classical dance, including recognition at national and international levels.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathak originated in North India and is characterised by intricate footwork, fast spins (chakkars), and expressive storytelling (abhinaya).

 

• Other prominent Kathak exponents include Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, and Shovana Narayan.

 

NOTE

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 1): A classical dance form from Tamil Nadu; noted exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale and Yamini Krishnamurthy.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 2): A classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh; noted exponents include Raja and Radha Reddy.

 

• Kathakali (Option 4): A classical dance-drama form from Kerala, known for elaborate costumes and facial makeup.

question: Which among the following is the oldest High Court in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Calcutta High Court, established on 1 July 1862 under the Indian High Courts Act, 1861, is the oldest High Court in India. (कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय — भारत का सबसे पुराना उच्च न्यायालय)

 

• It was followed shortly after by the Bombay High Court and the Madras High Court, also established in 1862.

 

• The Calcutta High Court has jurisdiction over the state of West Bengal and the Union Territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India currently has 25 High Courts, with the Allahabad High Court being the largest in terms of the number of judges.

 

• Under Article 214 of the Constitution, every state must have a High Court.

 

NOTE

 

• Allahabad (Option 1): Established in 1866, it is the largest High Court in India by judge strength, but not the oldest.

 

• Telangana (Option 2): The High Court for the State of Telangana was carved out from the common Andhra Pradesh High Court and became a separate court only in 2019.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Its current High Court was established in 2019 (after the earlier common High Court split with Telangana), making it a relatively recent High Court.

question: Article 76 of the Indian constitution is related with the office of which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Attorney General of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 76 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment, qualifications, duties, and remuneration of the Attorney General of India. (महान्यायवादी — भारत का शीर्ष विधि अधिकारी)

 

• The Attorney General is the highest law officer of the country, appointed by the President on the advice of the government, and must be qualified to be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

 

• The Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament (and their joint sittings) without the right to vote.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Attorney General is not a member of the Union Council of Ministers and does not have a fixed tenure specified in the Constitution — he holds office during the pleasure of the President.

 

• Similar law officer positions exist at the state level, called the Advocate General, provided for under Article 165.

 

NOTE

 

• Prime Minister of India (Option 1): The office and appointment of the Prime Minister is dealt with under Article 75, not Article 76.

 

• President of India (Option 2): The election of the President is dealt with under Article 54/55, and executive power under Article 53, not Article 76.

 

• Vice – President of India (Option 3): The election of the Vice-President is dealt with under Article 66, not Article 76.

question: The Pitts India Act of ______ distinguished between the commercial and political functions of the British East India Company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1784.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pitt's India Act, 1784, enacted under British Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger, distinguished between the commercial and political functions of the British East India Company. (पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट, 1784)

 

• It established a Board of Control in Britain to oversee the political affairs of the Company, while the Court of Directors continued to manage commercial affairs, thus creating a system of double government.

 

• This Act followed the earlier Regulating Act of 1773, which had first attempted to regulate the Company's affairs and created the office of the Governor-General of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Charter Act of 1833 later ended the East India Company's commercial activities altogether, making it purely an administrative body.

 

• The Government of India Act, 1858, transferred power from the East India Company directly to the British Crown after the Revolt of 1857.

 

NOTE

 

• 1818 (Option 1): Not the date of the Pitt's India Act; this period saw the conclusion of the Third Anglo-Maratha War.

 

• 1792 (Option 2): Not the date of the Pitt's India Act; no major constitutional act of this name was passed in this year.

 

• 1802 (Option 4): Not the date of the Pitt's India Act; the Treaty of Bassein with the Peshwa was signed this year.
